description: One round of improving a project's program: holds the program against a version an update writes of it — by a judge, on inputs that are said — and makes the new one the program where it is found the better. Run again, it is the next round.

parameters.project: string: the project to improve, by its name among the user's projects
parameters.check: string: the project that judges a run of it, by its name
parameters.inputs?: json: what to run it on — a list of arguments, [{…}, {…}], or that list as JSON text. What is found wanting of these is shown to the writer
parameters.heldBack?: json: more of them, never shown to the writer: where there are any, they alone decide
parameters.runs?: number: how many runs of each input (1)
parameters.ask?: string: what is wanted, in words — beside what was found wanting, or where nothing was
parameters.from?: string: what a run works on, where that is not the project itself — a directory, copied afresh for every run and handed to it as its workspace; {name} in it stands for the input's argument of that name
parameters.by?: string: how a version is found the better — good (how often, then the score) or score (the score, provided it is no less often good)
parameters.margin?: number: by how much a mean score has to be higher (0)
parameters.confirm?: number: how many times the runs that decide are made again where a version passes (0)
parameters.tell?: string: which runs the writer is told of — wanting, or all
parameters.write?: string: the project that writes the update, by its name (see examples/write-by-harness) — else whoever the configuration names, or pi's agent

returns.kept: boolean: whether a new version was made the program
returns.from?: number: the version the program was
returns.to?: number: the version that was written, and judged beside the program

before?.ok: number: how many runs were found good

after?.ok: number: how many runs were found good

returns.confirmed?: number: how many runs were made again to be sure of a version that passed
returns.remade?: number: how many runs failed and were made again
returns.why: string: what was decided, and by what

input.prompt: The loop: holds a project's program against the one an update writes, by a judge, and keeps the better.
